recommendations.headline: Spring Break wishlist · dry-season start · visa on arrival · Bonvoy-deep · superb veg
rationale: Early April is the START of Bali's dry season — weather turns in your favour exactly in this window, and the full 16-day break lets you stretch it
Wishlist destination (beach + culture + wellness — hits trip theme 4 directly) with visa-on-arrival for Indian passports; ~153 days out, so nothing to lock yet beyond watching fares
One of the best vegetarian-density profiles anywhere: Balinese-Hindu food culture, Ubud's dense plant-based scene, gado-gado, tempeh/tofu, and Indian restaurants in Seminyak
Deep Bonvoy footprint: The Ritz-Carlton Bali & St. Regis Bali (Nusa Dua), W Bali Seminyak, The Laguna Luxury Collection, Westin Nusa Dua, Renaissance Bali Uluwatu
Family pace: culture + rice-terrace + wellness base in Ubud, then a calm-beach decompress at Nusa Dua for kids 7 & 10
recommendations.est_cost: ₹4.5 – 6.5L (upper half of the ₹7L Lux cap — keep cabin economy and watch the resort tier)
recommendations.loyalty_play: Strongest Spring Break Bonvoy burn: ~4–5 award nights at Westin Nusa Dua / The Laguna (~45–60K/night) with 5th-night-free, OR cash on Titanium perks at The Ritz-Carlton / St. Regis to preserve balance. warnings: Mutually exclusive with Seoul — same Spring Break window; Bali is the warm beach+wellness option, Seoul the cooler culture-city one

Early April is the dry-season transition — mostly dry but plan one flexible indoor/spa day
Veg hazards: nasi goreng/mie goreng usually contain egg, and some dishes use shrimp paste (terasi) or fish sauce — specify lacto-veg, no egg, every time
